name: Donald Trump
_note: M2 benchmark expansion: President of the United States, first term 20 Jan 2017 to 20 Jan 2021 and second term from 20 Jan 2025. The most polarizing subject in the set; scored strictly on documented, uncontested events with conservative anchors, applying the same evidentiary standard as every other subject. International benchmark (reference head of government), not part of the ranked Malaysian class. C1 (coalition pivotality) and C2 (governance index) are jurisdiction-specific structural dimensions and are left unrecorded for this reference point rather than imputed; the benchmark anchors the conduct (Layer B) and integrity (A5) scales. Layer B (Editorial Panel) is a SINGLE-CODER provisional first-coder pass (coderScores length 1): each score is recorded and cited but NOT scored, normalized, or ranked, per methodology.validity.minCodersToScore=3. Citations verified to exist via search; article full text was not opened (environment fetch restriction), so facts rest on cross-outlet-corroborated search summaries and require primary-source reconfirmation before any independent panel finalizes the score.

metrics.justification: Factual status only, not a verdict on severity. Personal criminal conviction of record: a Manhattan jury found him guilty of 34 felony counts of falsifying business records (30 May 2024); sentenced to an unconditional discharge (10 Jan 2025), appeal pending. The three other criminal cases (federal classified-documents, federal election-interference, Georgia) were dismissed or dropped without a verdict on the merits. The Carroll defamation award and the New York civil-fraud matter (penalty later vacated on appeal) are civil liabilities, not criminal convictions. Recorded as factual status only.

metrics.justification: COVID-19 (2020): established the White House Coronavirus Task Force (29 Jan 2020), imposed travel restrictions, and declared a national emergency (13 Mar 2020), with outcome assessment sharply contested along partisan lines. In the April 2025 tariff episode, equities fell about 10% after the 2 Apr tariffs and he paused most reciprocal rates on 9 Apr. Documented mobilisation with contested/mixed outcomes (anchor 2).

metrics.justification: Enacted signature reforms into operative law: the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act (signed 22 Dec 2017, cutting the corporate rate to 21%) and the USMCA trade agreement (in force 1 Jul 2020, replacing NAFTA); the April 2025 reciprocal-tariff programme was materially diluted within a week of launch. Major reforms delivered, one diluted (anchor 3).

citation.title: Senate OKs North American Trade Deal To Replace NAFTA

metrics.justification: Signed the First Step Act (21 Dec 2018, Public Law 115-391), a bipartisan criminal-justice reform passed with supermajorities (Senate 87-12, House 358-36). Broader institutional-norms questions around him are politically contested and, lacking an uncontested official finding (the relevant cases were acquitted, dismissed, or upheld), are not scored here. Scored on the documented bipartisan instrument (anchor 3).

metrics.justification: Reversed the just-imposed reciprocal tariffs with a 90-day pause (9 Apr 2025), stating on the record that markets and people "were getting yippy ... a little afraid" and that "you have to be flexible" — a reversal explained in his own words, though whether the stated rationale was complete is debated (anchor 3).
